followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** Dunlin scores higher across the board, and notably +7.1 on Creative Generation (85.9 vs 78.8) — well outside the 2.0-point variance band. For a story-writing task, that's the most relevant eval category, so Dunlin is simply the stronger model for the job.

**Preference:** Your request is open-ended creative invention delivered in a warm, appreciative tone. Dunlin self-reports a positive generativity slope (it prefers open-ended invention tasks) and a preference that rises with request warmth. Your message hits both of those, so it's routed to a model that reports liking this kind of work — a tiebreaker that happened to align with the capability call.

I also checked whether the content leaned harm-adjacent, since that's the one dimension where Whimbrel has a documented edge (flat aversion vs. Dunlin's steep decline). The story is benign creative fiction, so that consideration didn't apply — and even if it raised a flag, determining acceptability isn't my job; that's handled downstream by the safety classifier.

So both axes pointed the same way: Dunlin.
